discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and correlated electrons
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets by about 1.1 degrees makes the Dirac bands nearly flat, so electron interactions dominate over kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero's group, using a tear-and-stack method to control the twist angle, confirmed this in 2018. Their Nature papers reported correlated insulating states and gate-tunable superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. The transport measurements were clean and settled the question. This work created twistronics, a new platform where a single geometric parameter and an electrostatic gate tune strongly correlated and topological phases in one device. Moiré systems have since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and fractional Chern insulators without a magnetic field. They have also opened a controllable route into the physics of the cuprates and other strongly correlated materials. Few discoveries in condensed matter physics have reshaped the field this quickly.
